disputed.proposed: Rename the right pole 'Scripture over tradition' and the top band 'Bible-only', because the 'Scripture alone' band was reachable only by respondents who deny the creeds any authority.
disputed.reason: The defect is real but it was caused by statements 13 and 15, not by the labels, and both have been rewritten. Under the revised items a Book of Concord or Westminster subscriber now scores 88-92 and reaches the top band, so the slogan is no longer handed only to biblicists. The proposed replacement would have created a new unfairness in its place: 'Bible-only' would be printed on Southern Baptist, Pentecostal, Bible-church and Restorationist respondents, who use 'sola scriptura' of themselves and would read Mathison's polemical coinage as a put-down. The half of the finding that survives on its own merits, bands[3] 'Scripture over tradition' (also asked for by catholic-23, presbyterian-10 and reformedcharismatic-9), has been applied.

disputed.proposed: Option (b): rename the poles 'Sacrament' and 'Ordinance' with bands ending 'ordinance-leaning', so that a 1689 Reformed Baptist at 67 is not told he is 'memorial-leaning'.
disputed.reason: Option (a) of the same blocker has been applied instead: statement 5 now tests whether God gives grace through baptism rather than who is baptized, so a 1689 subscriber scores 50 ('between sacramental and memorial') and the mis-score disappears without a rename. 'Memorial' also survives the holders'-own-vocabulary test that decided catholic-9: BF&M 2000 Art. VII says members 'memorialize the death of the Redeemer' and the AG Statement art. 6 calls the Supper 'a memorial'. 'Ordinance', by contrast, is used by both poles (LBC 30.7 calls the Supper 'that ordinance'; WLC 154 calls the sacraments ordinances), so it would name no pole.

disputed.proposed: Add a seventh axis (Church & World, or Church polity, or Church) or a seventh placement-only coordinate (the papacy; tongues as initial evidence) so that the peace churches, congregational polity, Rome versus Constantinople and Pentecostal versus charismatic are all measured.
disputed.reason: The demo is fixed at six axes and eighteen statements (apply.js warns on any other count, the page's radar has six spokes and the intro promises '18 statements, about 3 minutes'), and a coordinate the respondent answers but never sees on the compass is worse than an honest omission. What was applied instead: the Eastern Orthodox grace correction and the Catholic spirit correction (which widen the Rome/Constantinople gap from 13 to 18 units), the Pentecostal and charismatic coordinate changes (18.7 to 25.5 units), the 'peace church' qualifier on the Anabaptist entry, and a scope note under 'Nearest on the map' saying in the page's own voice that church government, the papacy and the peace-church convictions are not measured. The papacy and initial-evidence items are recommended for v1 in the report, where the item pool is being rebuilt anyway.

disputed.proposed: Rename the midpoint 'Neither agree nor disagree', add a sixth unscored 'Skip / don't know' option, score axes as 50 + 25 x mean over answered items, require a minimum number of answers per axis, and exclude unanswered axes from the headline and the distance.
disputed.reason: The harm this finding names, an all-Unsure respondent receiving a confident tradition match, is removed by two smaller changes that are applied: the tradition line is suppressed when all six axes sit within 10 of 50 (wesleyan-1), and the midpoint is relabelled 'Unsure / neither' (anabaptist-27). The rest is a scale redesign with per-axis minimums, an 'insufficient answers' state and a distance rescaled by sqrt(6/k), which cannot be expressed in this data file and is more instrument change than a three-minute demo needs. Recorded as a v1 recommendation.

disputed.proposed: Four to six statements per axis, keyed 2/2 or 3/3, so that acquiescence no longer produces a coherent profile.
disputed.reason: Correct and confirmed: agreeing with everything still yields 33/33/33/67/33/33 and the headline 'Monergist-leaning, sacramental-leaning, continuationist-leaning'. It cannot be fixed inside three items per axis, since 2:1 keying is forced, and the revised wording of every item is already fixed by other kept findings. Eighteen balanced, opposite-keyed candidates are supplied in candidate_statements so the v1 expansion is a selection exercise rather than a redesign.

disputed.proposed: Restructure key_passages per axis as {left, right, both} and render three labelled rows, as read_more already does, so the promise that these are 'the passages each side reaches for' is visible rather than asserted.
disputed.reason: This changes the shape of the data file and requires a matching change in renderHistory, which is outside a data revision; applying it half-way (a shape change with the old renderer) would throw. The substance of the promise has been met inside the flat lists instead: every axis is now balanced pole by pole (Grace 3-3 with two read both ways, Gifts 3-3-1, Table and Authority 4-4, Kingdom 3-3-3), and the Kingdom list is ordered canonically so the chips do not group by side. Recommended for v1 in the report.

disputed.proposed: Reword the bare 'Newman, An Essay on the Development of Christian Doctrine.' so it states a claim like every other entry.
disputed.reason: The entry itself was removed. historian-1's own fix offers dropping the Newman line if length matters, and orthodox-19 asks for Basil and Second Nicaea in its place so the tradition pole is not three-quarters Roman with no Eastern source; Newman remains the first title in read_more.left, where the Orthodox objection to the development thesis costs nothing.

Calvary Chapel is added; Independent Baptist is not. At the proposed coordinates it would sit about 20 units from the Bible church entry, which is the twin-tradition degeneracy this audit is otherwise removing, and the Bible church entry has been renamed 'Bible church (independent, dispensational)' so that bloc reads itself in the name.

disputed.proposed: Insert Calvin, Institutes II.10-11 (1559) as the one-covenant landmark alongside a reworded Westminster line.
disputed.reason: The 1646 line was reworded to state the one-covenant claim in Westminster's own words ('not two covenants of grace but one and the same'), which is what the finding's necessity fix asks for. Adding Calvin as well would give the left pole a fifth confessional entry against the right pole's four and duplicate a claim now stated in the entry immediately below it.

Only the broad-church note is applied. A third entry inside the already-tight Catholic/Orthodox/Anglican cluster would recreate the crowding that mockery-1 and survey-2 file as blockers, and the finding's own fairness and necessity verdicts recommend the note alone. An Anglo-Catholic respondent still sees 'Catholic (Roman and Eastern)' first, which the note now explains rather than leaving as a surprise.

disputed.proposed: Replace every straight apostrophe and quotation mark in the data and the HTML with typographic characters, on a page that already uses en dashes, middots, arrows and an ellipsis.
disputed.reason: Not applied. It is a global pass over strings that live in both the data file and the hand-written parts of the page, and the necessity lens dropped it as embarrassing nobody and mis-scoring nobody; doing it half-way (data only) would make the inconsistency more visible, not less. Worth one careful sweep at the v1 build, together with the other copy work listed in the report.
